sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is neutral today, with the VIX index up 1.95% to 15.70, still below the panic threshold of 20. The S&P 500 gains 0.41% to 7584.31, while the DXY loses 0.17% to 99.24. The market is awaiting upcoming macroeconomic data, such as the US GDP, due on July 29.

Il prezzo del petrolio scende dello 0.71% a $94.36, mentre l'oro guadagna lo 0.31% a $4489.60. La liquidità globale, misurata dal Global M2, è in espansione del 4.7% su base annua.
market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets are slightly up, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.41%. The bond market is stable, with TLT up 0.22%. Oil prices decline 0.71% to $94.36, while gold gains 0.31% to $4489.60. Global liquidity, measured by Global M2, is expanding at 4.7% YoY.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1.31%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.74%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.41%, il VIX è in aumento dell'1.95%. Il Dollar Index è in calo dello 0.17%, mentre l'oro è in rialzo dello 0.31% a $4489.6 l'oncia. Il petrolio è in calo dello 0.71% a $94.36 Il rendimento del decennale americano è in calo dello 0.31% al 4.47%, mentre il BTP 10Y italiano è stabile al 3.73%.

La situazione in Ucraina continua a rappresentare una sfida fiscale e finanziaria per il paese. Inoltre, le tensioni tra Iran e la comunità internazionale potrebbero avere un impatto sul mercato del debito globale.

Oggi saranno resi noti i dati sui Non-Farm Payrolls e il tasso di disoccupazione negli Stati Uniti. L'attenzione sarà focalizzata su questi dati per capire l'andamento del mercato del lavoro americano.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin scende dell'1,87% a 62.375 dollari. I flussi ETF mostrano una outflow di 396,6 milioni di dollari. Il movimento odierno potrebbe essere influenzato dai recenti dati macroeconomici che hanno aumentato l'incertezza sul mercato. Ethereum perde il 6,17% a mille 662 dollari, Solana cede il 5,55% a 65,19 dollari e BNB scende del 2,56% a 586,53 dollari. Il Fear & Greed Index è a 12, in zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Outlook breve: oggi monitoriamo i dati USA sul mercato del lavoro, con le Non-Farm Payrolls e il tasso di disoccupazione. 
  Invito articoli: Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. 
  Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed down 1.31%, Shanghai down 0.74%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. The S&P 500 closed up 0.41%, the VIX is up 1.95%. The Dollar Index is down 0.17%, while gold is up 0.31% at $4,489.6 per ounce. Oil is down 0.71% at $94.36 The 10-year US yield is down 0.31% to 4.47%, while the Italian 10Y BTP is stable at 3.73%. The situation in Ukraine continues to represent a fiscal and financial challenge for the country. Furthermore, tensions between Iran and the international community could have an impact on the global debt market. Today, the Non-Farm Payrolls and unemployment rate data will be released in the United States. Attention will be focused on these data to understand the trend of the American labor market. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin falls 1.87% to $62,375 ETF flows show an outflow of $396.6 million. Today's movement could be influenced by recent macroeconomic data that have increased uncertainty in the market. Ethereum loses 6.17% to $1,662, Solana drops 5.55% to $65.19 and BNB falls 2.56% to $586.53 The Fear & Greed Index is at 12, in the Extreme Fear zone, suggesting caution for investors. Short outlook: today we monitor US labor market data, with Non-Farm Payrolls and the unemployment rate.  Invitation to articles: To delve deeper into today's topics, you can find complete articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
articles.snippet: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. articles.title: Ukraine's fiscal and financial challenges
articles.snippet: As it faces the exigencies of an existential war, Ukraine is confronted with stark fiscal and financial policy trade-offs, despite the mitigation provided by large-scale external financial support. So far, its authorities have kept monetary and financial stability under control beyond a relatively brief initial episode of turmoil in 2022. What is the broad fiscal equation for Ukraine looking forward, taking into account uncertainties about European funding beyond 2027? Can domestic revenue be raised? articles.title: Norway Averts Offshore Strike as Workers and Industry Reach Deal
articles.snippet: Norway has narrowly avoided a strike at offshore oil platforms after trade unions and oil companies reached an agreement on wages in the early hours on Friday. The potential strike over wages could have threatened smooth operations offshore Norway, Western Europe's top oil and gas producer, at a time when the world is scrambling for oil and gas supply amid the Middle East crisis. Almost 8% of oil and gas workers offshore Norway early this week threatened to go on a strike from June 5 if trade union negotiations with industry fail to reach an agreement…

articles.title: U.S. Oil Shocks Don't Hit Like They Used To, Fed Study Finds
articles.snippet: The United States still feels oil shocks. It just doesn't feel them the way it did when America was dancing to disco and waiting in gas lines. If the Fed is right, the idea that every oil shock leads to recession is outdated. A new study from the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston finds that rising domestic oil production has fundamentally changed how higher crude prices ripple through the U.S. economy. The result is a country that remains vulnerable to energy inflation but is far less likely to suffer the kind of employment damage that accompanied…
